A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FuncBenchGen and the same underlying study. The main text, tables, figures, mathematical definitions, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven LLMs on generated function-calling tasks, including success rates, function-call counts, failure analyses, and mitigation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a mitigation comparison with 10 core nodes and detailed GPT-5 failure cases.

M1.justification: The DAG-based generator, type/subtype linking, function executor, and variable-reminder mitigation remain unchanged in Sections 3 and 4.6.1. The new Appendix A presents further details of the existing generator, rather than a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic multi-step function-calling tasks and graph conditions. Ten-core-node tasks were already evaluated in v1. The added taxi-reservation diagram illustrates an existing example; it is not a new real-world evaluation.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain GPT-5, GPT-5-mini, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Qwen3, GPT-4.1, and GPT-4.1-mini. The new mitigation comparison retains this set. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 extends the reported mitigation comparison from 5 to 10 core nodes in Figure 16, retaining the {0,10,20,40} connected-distractor conditions. This adds an experimental configuration; the existing model settings, metrics, depth grids, and function-call budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.7 adds two GPT-5 failure case studies, with annotated graphs in Figure 9 and a detailed execution trace in Appendix C.4, Figure 17. Figure 16 also tests mitigation on larger graphs. These are limited extensions of the existing failure and mitigation analyses.

E5.justification: v1 already reports five random graphs/trials and 95% confidence intervals. v2 Appendix A.2 explicitly identifies five different random seeds and labels illustrative seeds 0 and 100. This adds seed information without establishing more runs; the existing confidence-interval plot is retained as Figure 13.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 and the original plots retain their results. v2 Figure 16 adds success rates with and without mitigation for 10 core nodes, showing gains for most models. Section 4.7 adds qualitative failure findings. These supplement, rather than replace, the earlier results.

T1.justification: The task and dependency-graph definitions in Sections 3.1–3.2 are retained. Additional graph-generation details and explanations of the failure categories do not introduce new mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same benchmark and mitigation contributions and the same principal claims about reasoning models, dependency depth, distractors, and state tracking. The highlighted GPT-5 mitigation improvement remains 62.5% to 81.3%. Abstract compression does not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly identifies conditional logic and iteration as future extensions, making the control-flow boundary more explicit. The new case-study discussion explains failures through distractor-value substitution and omitted prerequisite calls, elaborating the existing state-tracking interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents adding up to 2n_core extra core-node edges and rejecting choices that exceed the depth constraint. Model identifiers, prompts, and main settings are retained. v2 removes the acceptance-contingent release promise, but both PDFs provide the same code link; an actual availability change is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of FOLIO, Multi-LogiEval, CRUXEval, program-runtime reasoning, HammerBench, LiveBench, and distraction by irrelevant context. A new code-reasoning paragraph distinguishes reasoning about code from using black-box tools. These broaden context without substantially redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract, expands selected explanations and related work, adds Section 4.7 and a graph-generation appendix, and relabels the previous appendices A/B as B/C. The header changes from preprint to ICLR 2026 publication. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Visual explanation expands substantially through the real-world DAG, graph-construction illustration, concrete generated graphs, annotated failure graphs, and full execution trace (Figures 3, 9–12, and 17). Figure 16 adds the 10-core mitigation chart. Existing tables and plots are retained, with renumbering and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added graph-generation details and annotated execution traces make the framework and failure analysis easier to understand and audit. Figure 16 provides additional evidence for mitigation beyond the original five-core-node comparison. These are useful incremental gains; the central method, main results, and evaluation scope remain stable.
